classification.summary: Proxy._exec() delegatecalled whitelisted handlers, and the Aave V2 handler in turn delegatecalled the Aave lending-pool proxy, so calling initialize() through that path wrote an attacker-controlled implementation into Furucombo's own storage and let the resulting evil contract pull every token users had approved to the Furucombo proxy.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/furucombo.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.

sources.note: onchain review: Furucombo Proxy 0x17e8ca1b created 2021-01-09 by 0xbcb909975715dc8fde643ee44b89e3fd6a35a259, not by attack sender 0xb624e2b1; victim/tx cross-checked against Coinspect learn-evm-attacks test/Business_Logic/Furucombo (loss there stated as $15m; rekt's leaderboard says $14m, used here). Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): the Proxy's EIP-1967 implementation slot was zero for its entire pre-incident life and only became 0x86765dde9304bea32f65330d266155c4fa0c4f04 at block 11940500 (2021-02-27T16:47:53Z) - the attacker's own setup transaction 0x6a14869266a1dcf3f51b102f44b7af7d0a56f1766e5b1908ac80a6a23dbaf449, sent by the same address 0xb624e2b10b84a41687caec94bdd484e48d76b212 19 minutes before the anchored tx - so that slot write is a consequence of the bug, not a pre-incident code change. The Proxy's own runtime keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation block 11618386 and the incident block 11940588, so the exploited code is the deployed Proxy code and deployment is the right basis.

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/furucombo.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
The legacy USD loss lacks uniformly structured valuation provenance.
